solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Extremely cheery stuff then ultimate in misery with me?

definitions.text: Extremely cheery stuff then ultimate in misery with me?

indicators.note: taken to extremes, a word yields only its two end letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
stuff is an old word for woven fabric

indicators.note: the ultimate thing in a word is its very last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reports swinging from very cheerful to miserable and wonders if that describes them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a cyclothyme swings between cheery highs and misery, and the speaker asks whether that is 'me'. 'then' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclothyme is a person prone to cyclothymia, a mild disorder of alternating elated and depressed moods, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Quickly America becomes tense in farewell to some Europeans

indicators.note: when one thing becomes another, a letter is swapped out for a new one

parts.note: the Italian goodbye
A is a standard abbreviation for America
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A note on how Americans hurry, as if a European goodbye were growing tense.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Italian goodbye, the A swaps for T. CITO is Latin, used on prescriptions and in English dictionaries as an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cito is a Latin adverb kept in English usage, chiefly medical, meaning with speed or promptly.

clue.text: A quid to duplicate the base of this column?

indicators.note: copying the bottom of something means repeating the closing run of letters at its foot

parts.note: the grid column holding this entry ends with the last four letters of the long entry at 14 down

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a pound to pay for copying the plinth of a classical column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quid' looks like a pound and 'column' like architecture, but the column is the one in the grid: 14 down, WAPENSCHAW, sits below this entry and ends in the same four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A quid is a lump of chewing tobacco, and chaw is the dialect name for exactly such a chewed plug.

clue.text: Work on island, however serve short periods in rear part of temple

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
IS is the map abbreviation for island
a clipped spelling of though
to do is to serve, as in 'that will do'
mo is a short moment, so these are brief spells of time

explanation.surface: A worker on an island must still serve brief stints in the back room of a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve short periods' reads like a prison sentence, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The opisthodomos is the back chamber or porch of a Greek temple, behind the main cella, often used as a treasury.

clue.text: Tapir touchy about seeing only every other animal in Central America

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the order runs backwards
looking at only every second item means alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A tapir gets prickly about only being allowed to see every other animal on its Central American range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tapir' looks like the animal being defined, but it is just raw letters; the real definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The hutia is a guinea-pig-like rodent native to the Caribbean islands, loosely placed here within the wider Central American region.

clue.text: Congolese city's openings for merchant banking upped jobs in start of fifth month?

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so each word contributes its initial letter

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words
the first of May, written with the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A banking report: a Congolese city's merchant banks are taking on more staff from early May.
explanation.walkthrough: The openings run further than they appear, through 'upped jobs in'; the start of the fifth month is a date, May the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Mbuji-Mayi is a large diamond-mining city in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, capital of Kasai-Oriental province.

clue.text: Shady mountainside capital of Caribbean country is seen last

indicators.note: a capital is a leading letter, marking which one is going to move
the leading letter turns up at the back instead, so the word rotates

parts.note: the island nation in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A travel note: a shady hillside where a Caribbean capital is the last place visited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a capital city, but it means the capital letter that starts the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubac is a geographical term for the slope of a mountain facing away from the sun, the opposite of the adret.

clue.text: French market town and grandmother each sheltering one with inner religiosity?

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it inside, and both items do so

parts.note: bourg is the French word for a market town
the Roman numeral
an informal word for a grandmother
the Roman numeral again, used a second time

explanation.surface: A French town and a granny both give refuge to someone of deep private faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The single 'one' is used twice, once inside each of the two pieces. The question mark flags a loose description rather than a dictionary gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourignians followed Antoinette Bourignon, a seventeenth-century Flemish mystic who taught that true faith lay in inward feeling, not outward forms.

clue.text: Possible proviso in treaty before intelligence on direction of third Axis military strategist

parts.note: a treaty's terms and conditions are set out section by section
wit in its sense of mental sharpness
in three-dimensional coordinates the third axis is labelled z

explanation.surface: A wartime picture: a treaty proviso, military intelligence and the Axis powers, all fitting a strategist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axis' with its capital letter suggests the WWII alliance, but it is the third axis of a graph. 'intelligence' is mental sharpness, not spying.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl von Clausewitz was the Prussian general whose book On War became a founding text of military theory.

clue.text: Meadow flower in goblet with its rim covered by dry Bacardi, say

indicators.note: the outer edge is covered over and something new sits in place of it

parts.note: a chalice is a drinking cup on a stem
TT is teetotal, a dry person who abstains from alcohol
Bacardi is a brand of this spirit, so 'say' marks an example

explanation.surface: A cocktail scene: a flower dropped into a glass with a dry rum served around its rim.
explanation.walkthrough: The cup's first and last letters are its rim, and they give way to the two letters for teetotal, which seems odd beside the rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Thalictrum is the botanical genus of meadow rue, flowering plants of the buttercup family found in damp grassland.

clue.text: Ceremonial exchange of gifts, several given away in the middle of Kumbh Mela

indicators.text: several given away in the middle of
indicators.note: giving things away from the centre leaves a gap there, so a run of letters goes

parts.note: the name of the Hindu pilgrimage festival

explanation.surface: Gifts are handed out among the crowds at an enormous Hindu festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Five central letters go, leaving the first two and last two. The Kumbh Mela is a mass Hindu pilgrimage to bathe in a sacred river.
explanation.definitionFit: The kula ring is a ceremonial exchange system of the Trobriand Islands, where shell necklaces and armbands circulate between trading partners.

clue.text: Cause of melanoma on arm during day since rising state of panic

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls inside it
in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the abbreviation for Tuesday
as in 'as it was raining'
ultraviolet light from the sun causes skin cancer
to arm troops is to equip them

explanation.surface: A health scare: a mole on someone's arm, panic building by the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a body part beside melanoma but is a verb. The day and 'since' go upwards together, then the other two pieces sit in their middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means 'save himself who can', a general stampede or rout, so it names a condition of chaotic panic.

clue.text: Limits of short part of arm holding back Shankar's string instrument

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the radius is one of the two forearm bones

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction

parts.note: Ravi Shankar, the Indian sitar player

explanation.surface: A sitar maestro's string instrument, played with a short part of the arm held back.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous sitarist suggests his sitar is the answer, but he only lends his first name, written backwards inside the forearm bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stradivarius is a violin or cello made by Antonio Stradivari, the most prized makes of bowed stringed instrument.

clue.text: Hot lift of pickle among more modest fruit

indicators.note: being among others places something in their midst

parts.note: the comparative of coy, shy
H for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting something turns it to read from the bottom up

parts.note: a pickle and a mire are both a mess or plight

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene where hot pickle is spooned in among a plate of quieter fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' looks like food beside 'fruit', but it means a fix or predicament here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherimoyer is a variant spelling of cherimoya, the custard apple of the Andes with creamy white flesh.

clue.text: Hand over the four points, taking tea in S African shooting competition

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end

parts.note: a paw is an informal word for a hand

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

parts.note: the four compass points, east, north, south and west
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: At a South African shoot, a competitor hands over the four points and takes tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand over' looks like one phrase meaning give up, but splits into a word and its reversal signal; 'points' here are compass directions, not scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Wapenschaw, originally a Scottish muster of armed men, survives in South Africa as the name for a rifle-shooting meeting.

clue.text: The reason a single mother (not wife) makes sponge

indicators.note: saying something is not there means it is taken away

parts.note: asking the reason is asking why
taken as written
single as in solitary
an informal word for a mother
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Explaining why an unmarried mother is the one wiping down with a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket sounds like a comment on her marital status, but it takes the letter for wife out of the opening piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyalonema is a genus of deep-sea glass sponges, anchored by a long twisted rope of silica spicules.

clue.text: Maybe a pectoral cross's enclosure left in religion for Masses?

parts.note: enc. is the abbreviation written on letters for an enclosure

indicators.note: something placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: Marx called religion the opium of the people
L for left

explanation.surface: A churchy picture: a bishop's cross kept in an enclosure, with religion offered at Masses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses' has a capital to suggest the Catholic service, but it is Marx's masses, for whom religion was a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: An encolpium is a small reliquary or cross worn on the breast, so a pectoral cross is one kind; 'Maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Supplier of grapes with mouldiness

parts.note: grapes grow on a vine
W is an abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's complaint: the grapes came with mould on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplier of grapes' sounds like a merchant, but it is the plant itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinew is an archaic word for mould or mustiness, the furry growth on stale bread or damp things.

clue.text: Measure of infectiousness not advanced in level or receding

indicators.note: saying something is not present means it is dropped

parts.note: to level a building is to raze it
A is an abbreviation for advanced

indicators.note: to recede is to go back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Epidemiology talk: the rate of infection has stopped advancing and is levelling off or falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'level' is a verb, to demolish, not a reading on a chart; drop the letter for advanced from it.
explanation.definitionFit: R-zero, the basic reproduction number, is the average count of new cases each infected person causes in a susceptible population.

clue.text: Half of clan wearing fashion designer's tinsel

indicators.note: taking half a word keeps only its first two of four letters

parts.note: the front half of the word
dressed in, as in 'in a hat'
Mary Quant, the British designer who popularised the miniskirt

explanation.surface: Half a clan is decked out in a designer's glittery tinsel.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was the 1960s London fashion designer behind the miniskirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinquant means glittering with gold or silver, and as a noun it is tinsel or imitation gold leaf.

clue.text: East Londoner's sweet bun satisfied judge that is swallowing outsized seed capsule

indicators.note: whatever is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a need is met when it is satisfied
J is the abbreviation for judge
i.e., Latin id est
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
a boll is the seed pod of cotton or flax

explanation.surface: A Cockney eats a sweet bun, and a contented judge swallows an oversized seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Londoner' suggests a Cockney, but East London is a city in South Africa, where this Afrikaans bun belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosbolletjie is an Afrikaans name for a sweet bun leavened with fermenting grape must, baked across South Africa.

clue.text: Perhaps an early visitor to London galleries, conceivably

definitions.meaning: an early is an early potato, and this is a slang word for any potato
a made-up word for someone who goes to the Tate galleries

explanation.surface: Someone first through the doors when London's galleries open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' looks like an adjective for the visitor but is a noun, a new potato. 'conceivably' flags that the second meaning is coined: Tate plus the -ER ending of a doer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tater is informal slang for a potato, and an early is a variety of potato lifted in late spring or early summer.

clue.text: Mediterranean boat espionage organisation's capsized

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is upside down, and in a down entry that means bottom to top

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A spy agency's boat overturns in the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S contributes its letter rather than meaning 'is' or 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saic is a Levantine ketch, a two-masted trading vessel once common in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Location of gardens large and marvellous

parts.note: Kew Gardens, the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London
L for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Praise for a garden site that is big and wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is a district of west London, home of the Royal Botanic Gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Kewl is a jokey slang spelling of cool, used as an exclamation of approval meaning great or excellent.

clue.text: Questionable circles spurning duke affected upper-class people

indicators.note: going round in a circle brings you back the other way
to spurn is to reject, so a letter is thrown out

parts.note: shady as in dubious or suspect
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Dubious social circles snubbing a duke, full of affected toffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' looks like a noun for social sets, but it is a verb telling the letters to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: Yah is British slang for a posh person, mocking the upper-class drawl of 'yah' for yes.

clue.text: Historically, stocks let it out, breaking occupier's contract

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it

parts.note: a tenant occupies a property under a lease

indicators.note: things turned out are set loose and fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Property talk: a stock of flats let out, with the tenant breaking the lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' looks like goods or shares, but means the old punishment frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Little-ease was a historical place of confinement, a cell or set of stocks too cramped to stand or lie in comfortably.

clue.text: Aftermath of knight fighting in retreat

indicators.note: a retreating army goes backwards, so the order is turned round

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
war is armed fighting

explanation.surface: The aftermath of battle, with a knight in combat falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aftermath' suggests the result of the fighting, but it is the farming sense, so the definition is quite separate from the battle picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawn is a dialect word for aftermath in its original farming sense, the second growth of grass after mowing.

clue.text: I'm doubtful terror turned calm, except for case occurring in a building

indicators.note: something turned round faces the opposite way
the case of a word is its outside, and leaving that off removes the first and last letters

parts.note: the hesitant noise of someone unsure
a little terror is a badly behaved child
placid means calm and untroubled

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether their terror has really turned to calm while shut indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' sits right after 'terror' but acts on the calm word, once its outer letters are gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbratical means keeping to the shade, hence secluded and indoor, staying within a building rather than out in public.
